newsitem.title: USA: US March spot natgas more than $1 under Feb index.
newsitem.headline: US March spot natgas more than $1 under Feb index.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices for March 1 delivery slid more than a $1 per mmBtu under February indices on Tuesday, as mild weather and ample storage supplies weakened demand significantly.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices for March were mostly in the low-to-mid $1.70s, down from February indices in the $2.80s.

February prices for Wednesday delivery fell more than five cents to the low-$1.80s as forecasts called for much warmer temperatures across the eastern two-thirds of the U.S. through at least this weekend.
In south Texas, March prices were in the low-$1.60s, down about $1.10 from February indices.
In the Permian basin, March gas prices slid about $1 under February indices into the $1.54-1.60 range.
Permian prices for Wednesday delivery edged lower into the mid-$1.70s.
Southern California border prices for March hovered in the mid-to-high $1.50s, as few buyers entered the market.
Bonneville Power Administration was offering 200 megawatts (MW) of power for Wednesday after being absent from the market on Monday.

However, BPA said Washington Public Power Supply's 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power unit is expected to be taken off line this Saturday for maintenance and refueling, which is much earlier than expected due to the abundant hydro supply.

In the Midcontinent, March prices were talked mostly in the low-to-mid $1.60s, down about $1.15 from February 1 levels. Demarcation was quoted around $1.70, while Chicago city-gate gas sold for next month was in the high-$1.80s, sources said.
In the East, New York city-gate prices for March 1 dove into the $2.08-2.12 area, down about $1.50 from February indices. February prices fell at least 10 cents to the $2.10-2.15 range.
Withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association report have ranged from about 80 to 113 bcf.
